findings.title: Max upload size hardcoded, ignoring site settings
findings.body: The client-side file size check previously read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, honoring the admin-configured per-type (image/attachment) limits. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB for every upload type. This removes admin configurability: sites configured with a smaller (or larger) `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` will now get an incorrect client-side limit that no longer matches the server-side setting used elsewhere (e.g. `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` in `uploads_controller.rb`). This can let users attempt uploads the server will reject (bad UX) or block uploads the admin actually wants to allow.

findings.title: 413 error message now reports a hardcoded size instead of actual configured limit
findings.body: In `displayErrorForUpload`, the max size shown to the user for HTTP 413 (entity too large) responses was previously `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`, reflecting the real server-configured limit. It is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. If the admin has configured a different `max_image_size_kb`, the error message shown to users will state an incorrect maximum size, causing confusion.

findings.title: URL-based upload download limit hardcoded, bypassing configured max image size
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` was changed to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. This decouples the API-driven URL download size cap from the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb` setting, allowing downloads up to 10MB regardless of what the admin has configured (potentially larger than intended), and is inconsistent with the rest of the method which still checks `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` for the downsizing loop.

findings.title: Downsize failures are silently ignored in the retry loop
findings.body: The new retry loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` without checking its return value. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` (invoked under the hood) returns `false` and logs an error when the `convert`/`gifsicle` shell command fails or raises, but here that failure is never checked. If the command fails partway (e.g. ImageMagick not installed, corrupt source, unsupported format) while writing to the same path as the source (`from == to`), the loop will still decrement `attempt` and continue, and ultimately the method proceeds to create the Upload from whatever is left in `tempfile.path`, which could be a corrupted, zero-byte, or unmodified oversized file — with no error surfaced to the caller.

findings.title: No fallback when image cannot be downsized under the max size within 5 attempts
findings.body: After the `while attempt > 0 ...` loop exits, there is no check whether `tempfile.size` is still over `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. If 5 rounds of 80% downsizing are not enough to bring the file under the configured limit (e.g. for certain image types that don't compress well), the code silently proceeds to create the Upload with a file that still exceeds the configured maximum, defeating the purpose of the size check and potentially bypassing storage constraints.

findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently shadows the original method, breaking its public signature
findings.body: Two class methods named `downsize` are now defined: one at line 145 with signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and a new one at line 149 with signature `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the second definition completely replaces the first — the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` version becomes dead, unreachable code. Any existing caller elsewhere in the codebase that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` with width and height as separate arguments (the previously documented/public signature) will now raise an `ArgumentError` (wrong number of arguments) because the surviving method only accepts a single `dimensions` string plus 3 positional args. This is a breaking API change for any code that wasn't updated alongside this PR, and the leftover dead method should be removed rather than shadowed.

findings.title: Missing tests for changed downsize/optimize behavior and new auto-downsizing feature
findings.body: The PR changes the public signature of `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` (switching from separate width/height args to a `dimensions` string) and adds a new auto-downsizing retry loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`, but no test changes are included. Given the signature collision bug and the silent-failure risk in the retry loop, this change is particularly risky to ship without unit/controller tests covering: successful downsizing under the limit, failure to downsize within 5 attempts, and compatibility of any other callers of `OptimizedImage.downsize`.
